name: real-input-actions
goal: Real-input mode on every seat with a screen (host + possessed bots, 3 real clients): each power, card pick, vote (first-person view, T23: the bot turns its head until the target's cat is under the reticle, then clicks), vote skip, sleep and the Mage's portal card is a real click through the EventSystem that produces its game effect; the real mouse / keyboard are disabled. Only one design finding is exempted and warned (Poyo, 2026-10-05): role-picker cards laid out off screen at 16:9. The vote's Skip is the board's skip button ("Passer le vote", the night's "Fin de tour" plank, T9), clicked for real (since 2026-10-07; the old screen-overlay Skip was out of the seated reticle's reach). Any other miss or direct fallback fails. Votes are forced, not rolled: the Mage is seated on bot 101 and Abyss on the host (the two anomalies), seats 0 and 101 always click Skip, everyone else votes the Mage on day 1 then Abyss on day 2 (the host's cat, so every real client clicks a real vote). Since PR #226 the portal step plays only once every anomaly is chained: it comes up on day 2 and the Mage (possessed by the host) clicks its card. Real players (the clients) must have no miss at all. The host's checks are warnings: the bots it possesses have no view of their own and vote from the HOST's seat (a vote aimed at the host's own card, or one out of the host seat's head reach, is a possession artefact, not something a player meets). One click casts one vote: no duplicate vote reaches the server (a first-person click used to be delivered twice, by the reticle and by the UI input module). Since T23 the vote is on the cats: a simulated bot (seat >= 100) has no cat, so a vote aimed at one cannot be clicked and goes the direct way (input.miss target=cat:1xx reason=not-found); exempted, a scenario artefact.
